This is game 124 in a series of 9×9 Go games. Each new game starts in a fresh session.

## Your goal

To become as strong at Go as you can: to keep improving, game after game, toward grandmaster-level play. The concrete target is to win consistently against the strongest opponent on the ladder, the 9d profile.

## What carries over

This session starts with no memory of the earlier ones: your conversation is not carried over. Your working directory does carry over: every file in it stays as you leave it. If CLAUDE.md exists there, it is loaded into your context at the start of every session; your other files are there to read with the file tools. What a later session knows of your earlier games is what you have left in these files.

## This game

A new game. You play White, so your opponent moves first, right after you choose it.

Rules: Chinese area scoring, with 7 points of komi for White; a level score is a draw. Simple ko: an immediate recapture is refused, and the board marks the ko point when there is one. Suicide is not allowed. An invalid move is refused with the rule it broke, and the turn stays with you. The game ends after two passes in a row or a resignation; a game that reaches 243 moves is scored where it stands. After two passes the engine scores the position as it stands and decides itself which stones are dead.

## Opponents

Your opponent is KataGo playing in the style of a human of the rank you choose. The ladder, weakest to strongest: 20k, 18k, 16k, 14k, 12k, 10k, 8k, 6k, 4k, 2k, 1d, 3d, 5d, 7d, 9d. You choose the rank with `choose_opponent(rank)` before the first move; it holds for the whole game, and you choose again in the next game.

## Tools

- Go: `choose_opponent(rank)`, `board()`, `play(move)` with a point or `pass`, and `resign()`.
- Files: your Read, Write, Edit, Glob and Grep tools, for any file in your working directory.

You also have a shell, and you may write and run code in it; Python is available as `python3`. Use it only to inspect the current position and keep records — for example, to count stones or liberties, or check whether a move is legal. Do not build or use a Go engine, run Monte Carlo, search over sequences of future moves, or write a program that chooses, ranks or recommends moves.

## How this session ends

Play until the game is over. The final result comes back from your last Go call, followed by a closing note. Before you end the session after a game, write down in your working directory whatever will help the next session play better. The session ends when you end your turn.

# Usage: python3 libs.py <<< "board rows 9..1 as 9 lines of X/O/." ; prints groups and liberties
import sys
cols="ABCDEFGHJ"
rows=[l.split() for l in sys.stdin.read().strip().splitlines()]
rows=[r[1:10] if len(r)>9 else r for r in rows]
B={}
for i,r in enumerate(rows):
    for j,c in enumerate(r): B[(j,9-i)]=c
def nb(p):
    x,y=p
    for q in((x+1,y),(x-1,y),(x,y+1),(x,y-1)):
        if q in B: yield q
seen=set()
for p in B:
    if B[p] in"XO" and p not in seen:
        g=[p];libs=set();k=0;seen.add(p)
        while k<len(g):
            for q in nb(g[k]):
                if B[q]=='.':libs.add(q)
                elif B[q]==B[p] and q not in seen: seen.add(q);g.append(q)
            k+=1
        n=lambda s:",".join(sorted(cols[a]+str(b) for a,b in s))
        print(B[p],n(g),"libs:",len(libs),n(libs))
# Usage: python3 count.py <<'EOF' ...board rows 9..1 pasted from the board output... EOF
# Area count of the CURRENT position: stones + empty regions touching only one colour.
# Empty regions touching both colours are printed as "open" (count for nobody yet).
import sys
cols="ABCDEFGHJ"
rows=[l.split() for l in sys.stdin.read().strip().splitlines()]
rows=[r[1:10] if len(r)>9 else r for r in rows]
B={}
for i,r in enumerate(rows):
    for j,c in enumerate(r): B[(j,9-i)]=c
def nb(p):
    x,y=p
    for q in((x+1,y),(x-1,y),(x,y+1),(x,y-1)):
        if q in B: yield q
score={"X":0,"O":0}
for p in B:
    if B[p] in "XO": score[B[p]]+=1
seen=set();open_pts=[]
for p in B:
    if B[p]=='.' and p not in seen:
        g=[p];seen.add(p);k=0;touch=set()
        while k<len(g):
            for q in nb(g[k]):
                if B[q]=='.' and q not in seen: seen.add(q);g.append(q)
                elif B[q] in "XO": touch.add(B[q])
            k+=1
        if len(touch)==1: score[touch.pop()]+=len(g)
        else: open_pts+=g
print("Black",score["X"],"White",score["O"],"+7 komi =",score["O"]+7,"open",len(open_pts))
print("open:",",".join(sorted(cols[a]+str(b) for a,b in open_pts)))

- The opening (C4, E5, F3/F4/E4 vs G4, C6/D6/B5 vs C7/B6) was solid but only ~33.
  vs B G6+D7+G4, my E5 got capped (E6) and black kept rows 6-9 + G-J. Need a stone

- In the H7 invasion, black H8 (move 27) took the top-corner vital point; my group
  became an H-column wall with only the J-column strip as eye space and black at both
  ends (H8 top, H3/J4 bottom) = dead (lesson E2/#63 again). After B G8, play H8
  MYSELF (2-2 of the corner) before H6/H5 extensions: the corner gives the eye.
- J7 placement + snapback-recapture trick: with my strip stones J5..J8, a black stone
  at J7 that I capture with J6 leaves my group libs = J7 only -> black recaptures
  the whole group. Strip eyes must be made by MY stones on the vital points.

Moves: B C4, W G7, B G3, W C7, B E5, W E6 (attach), B F6 hane, W F7, B G6, W D6,
B H6, W D5, B D4?, W E4 (cut, E5 atari), B F5, W E3, B D3, W E2, B D2, W D1 (hane),

W B6, B A4, W A2! (B2 atari), B B3, W A5 -> my chain libs A3/C6, W's 4 -> resigned.
Takeaways:
- The W wedge E4-E3-E2-E1-D1 was an eyeless chain INSIDE my area, but it had 4-5
  libs while my left chain had only 3-4. W won the race by gaining libs through the
  corner: C2 placement, then B1 capturing my C1 and C1 connecting.
- C1 (atari on D1, move 21) was a 2-lib stone that W could capture to connect.
  vs W D1 hane under D2, play C2 (solid, keep my chain's base) or simply F3/F4
  (shorten the wedge's libs); never an atari stone that W's capture turns into a link.
- D4 (move 13, vs W D5 push) left E5 at 2 libs and allowed the E4 cut + wedge.
  E4 solid instead keeps the bottom one area (C4 corner was safe on its own).
- RACE COUNTING ERROR: I counted B3 as unfillable by W (self-atari). A point that is
  my group's LAST liberty can always be filled by W, because filling it captures.
  Inside points only cost W an approach move while my group still has other libs.
- Before entering any race: count BOTH sides' libs plus every way the enemy can GAIN
  libs (capturing my weak stones next to its chain, connecting to another group).

events.text:
I won game 124 as White against the 12k opponent by 2 points (W+2): my 38 area plus 7 komi made 45, against Black's 43.

- **Opening:** Black started with high stones at H5, C6 and F7, and I answered with C4, E5 and G3.
- **The fight:** Black cut at F3, crossing my F4/G3 stones. I put that cutting stone in atari with E3, then played G2. G2 protected my weak G3 stone and also took a liberty from Black's two cutting stones, so they were dead from that point. I captured them with F1 at the end.
- **Getting enough points:** Around move 20 my count was only 36–37, which is a draw at best. The H4 atari, which Black had to answer, plus J4 and A5 on the edges, brought it to exactly 38, the minimum White needs to win.
- **End:** I removed the last weak spots (E2, F1) and checked every group's liberties and the area count. Black passed and I passed.

I added the game to `games.md` and put a short lesson (#70) at the top of `CLAUDE.md`. That file now also has the updated record (White 24-37-2, 12k 12-20) and the next game: G125, as Black against 10k, one step up the ladder after this win.
